- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >2.5x recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or use moving average to dampen.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust upward by 5–15% if sentiment remains low but price shows momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply a 10–20% upward bias for short-term horizons.
- For long-term forecasts (15+ days), model shows mean-reversion bias; apply a 5–10% downward correction if recent sentiment is mixed or declining.
- When sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast weights for smoother transitions.
